blocks.text: **The problem.** Given an array `nums` sorted in increasing order, build a **height-balanced** binary search tree from it — for every node, the heights of its two subtrees differ by at most one. Any balanced answer is accepted.

blocks.alt: The sorted array -10, -3, 0, 5, 9. The middle value 0 becomes the root; the left half -10, -3 builds the left subtree (middle -10, then -3 as its right child) and the right half 5, 9 builds the right one the same way. The result has height 3.

elements.text: the middle value is the root; each half builds a subtree

blocks.text: Why not just insert them in order?

Inserting a sorted list one value at a time makes every new value the right child of the last one: a **chain** of height n, the worst possible BST. The fix is to choose the root first — the **middle** value splits the rest into two halves whose sizes differ by at most one, and that keeps every level balanced.

blocks.caption: Each call takes a range of the array, makes its middle value the node, and recurses on both halves.

blocks.text: **Time O(n), space O(log n)** for the recursion (the tree it builds is balanced, so the depth is log n). Passing indexes instead of slicing the array keeps it O(n) — slicing would copy and cost O(n log n).
2. Iterative with a stack of ranges
The same splits without recursion: keep a stack of jobs "build nums[lo..hi] as the left/right child of this parent".

blocks.code:
def sorted_array_to_bst(nums):
    if not nums:
        return None
    mid0 = (len(nums) - 1) // 2
    root = TreeNode(nums[mid0])
    stack = [(root, 0, mid0 - 1, "left"), (root, mid0 + 1, len(nums) - 1, "right")]
    while stack:
        parent, lo, hi, side = stack.pop()
        if lo > hi:
            continue
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
        node = TreeNode(nums[mid])
        setattr(parent, side, node)       # attach, then split this range
        stack.append((node, lo, mid - 1, "left"))
        stack.append((node, mid + 1, hi, "right"))
    return root

blocks.text: **Time O(n), space O(log n)** — the stack holds at most about two jobs per level.

blocks.alt: Recursion on ranges: O(n) time, O(log n) space. Stack of ranges: O(n) time, O(log n) space.

items: **Even length** — two middles; either choice is balanced (round down gives one shape, round up the mirror).
**Negative values** — nothing changes; only positions matter.
